props.context_text: One man gambling all of it on Wall Street.

props.text: Within thirty days the entire financial system stopped.

props.name: WILLIAM DUER
props.title: Fmr. Assistant Secretary of the Treasury

props.text: He knew every bond price — and used it to blow up the market that had just been born.

props.label: TREASURY REPORT, OCT. 1790
props.caption: Two new federal bonds: the Sixes (6%) and the Threes (3%).

props.text: Duer partnered with Alexander Macomb to corner the market in US debt.
Scrip for Bank of the United States shares went on sale — the city went into a buying frenzy.

props.context_text: Par value — thirty days after the scrip sale.

props.label: S.U.M. CHARTER, PATERSON N.J.
props.caption: Duer's industrial company — and his personal line of credit.

props.text: He personally raised five hundred thousand dollars to capitalize it — then borrowed it back for himself.
Bank of the United States shares rose from five hundred twenty-eight dollars to seven hundred twelve in the same weeks.
The Bank noticed. Its cash reserves stood at seven hundred six thousand dollars.
So the Bank slammed the brakes — discounts cut hard, credit vanishing exactly when Duer needed it most.
Credit vanished exactly when Duer needed to roll over his loans.

props.label: S.U.M. COMPTROLLER'S DEMAND
props.caption: Duer's unauthorized loan, discovered and called in.

props.text: Duer had nowhere left to borrow.
On March 9, William Duer stopped paying his debts.

props.label: DUER TO HAMILTON, MAR. 11 1792
props.caption: "Issued by my agent during my absence from this City."

props.text: On March 23, 1792, Duer was arrested and sent to the New Gaol debtors' prison in Manhattan.
Mobs surrounded the building. One creditor collected fifteen hundred dollars from him at gunpoint.

props.context_text: "Not a rich man in the City left standing."

props.text: Hamilton began America's first lender-of-last-resort operation.
Treasury purchases pushed into banks across the Northeast. By May, the market had stabilized.
Two months later, twenty-four brokers signed the Buttonwood Agreement outside 68 Wall Street.

props.label: BUTTONWOOD AGREEMENT, MAY 17 1792
props.caption: Founding document of the New York Stock Exchange.

props.text: William Duer died in debtors' prison seven years later. He never paid a cent.

props.label: TWENTY-SEVEN YEARS LATER
props.sub_hook: The country did it again — at national scale.

props.label: CHARTER EXPIRED, 1811
props.caption: Five years with no central bank — state banks print freely.

props.text: The Second Bank of the United States opened in Philadelphia, 1817 — eighteen branches, almost no oversight.

props.context_text: War-torn Europe needed American cotton, wheat, corn, tobacco.

props.text: Public land sold at two dollars an acre, quarter down — speculators borrowed hard against it.
Then the Second Bank reversed course to protect its own reserves — loans cut hard within a year.
Note circulation fell from ten million to four million.
British mills switched to cheaper Indian cotton. European harvests recovered.

props.name: LANGDON CHEVES
props.title: President, Second Bank of the United States

props.text: State banks that couldn't redeem their notes failed outright. Foreclosures swept the cotton belt.
Pennsylvania land dropped from one hundred fifty dollars an acre in 1815 to thirty-five dollars in 1819.
Across New York, Philadelphia, and Baltimore combined, roughly fifty thousand people were out of work.
The depression dragged on into 1821. Agricultural prices fell by half.

props.label: MCCULLOCH v. MARYLAND, 1819
props.caption: The Court upholds the Bank — just as the country turns against it.

props.text: The resentment seeded Andrew Jackson's Bank War — and the Bank's death in 1836.
The second one rewrote how Americans thought about banks for a generation.
Cheap credit. A rising price. Someone convinced the rise would never stop.
Both ended the same way — a central bank pulling money out faster than it went in.
Wall Street got its stock exchange. The country got its first taste of a national depression.

props.title: THE LEDGER DOESN'T FORGET.
props.subtext: It just waits for the next name to fill in the blank.
